shared_conventions.screen_side: screen-left / screen-right / centred in frame, always as the audience sees it, taken from the anchor_xy and gaze fields of the shot's own composition.json. Screen side is a projection of the frame, never a world direction; world position is carried by the landmark clause.
shared_conventions.fragment_grammar: space_fragment_en = <pose word> + <relation to a scene landmark> + <screen side> + <facing>, in that order, one sentence, English, no numeric coordinates, no camera-move terms, no colour codes, 25 words maximum. The pose word opens the fragment so the whitebox compiler and the video prompt both lock the body attitude.
shared_conventions.landmark_vocabulary: Landmark words are copied letter for letter from the shot's scene layout.json name_en. No translation, paraphrase, pluralisation or shortening. Scale phrases ("ten inches high", "two feet high") are scale, not coordinates, and follow the blocking_map offset_en wording.
shared_conventions.pose_source: pose is copied from shot_list.json shots[].poses[<id>].pose and is never overridden here; where a shot changes attitude inside its own duration the change is carried in path[]/beats[] and the fragment names both states.
shared_conventions.offscreen_presence: Characters who are in the scene but not in the frame are recorded in offscreen_presence[] with their map position and carry no space fragment, because blocking_bound binds in-frame characters only. Presence and visibility are judged separately.
shared_conventions.intent_layer: performance (dialogue-anchored) carries goal/objective, arc_from + arc_to + emotional_arc, trigger {line_ref, word}, forbidden_early + no_early_reaction, end_state. Both the host-canonical field names and the work order's aliases are written so nothing downstream has to guess. No FACS codes, no camera language, no prompt phrasing.

deviations_and_open_items.detail: The work order requires the intent layer on every shot where a character acts, and requires trigger to be anchored to a finalised dialogue line. On a silent shot those two requirements cannot both hold, and writing a dialogue-anchored trigger into a silent shot would make the downstream performance_bound check (code/performance_bound_check.py) report the trigger word as absent from that shot's segment.
deviations_and_open_items.resolution: Dialogue shots carry performance with a dialogue-anchored trigger (33 blocks, exactly the host-checked shape). Silent acting shots carry the same intent fields under performance_beat, whose trigger is an action beat with a timestamp inside the shot (67 blocks). performance_bound reads only performance, so the silent shots add no false violations while still handing the prompt station a full intent layer.

deviations_and_open_items.detail: The three CRE-001 entries (sh008, sh010, sh012) carry an animal_discipline field instead of an intent layer: true gait, true scale, no clothing, no pause, no look to camera and no look at Alice.
deviations_and_open_items.rationale: CRE-001 is the real mute quadruped and is explicitly directed as an animal rather than a performer; giving it an objective and an emotional arc would contradict that discipline. CHAR-white-rabbit, who is a character, does carry the full intent layer in all eight of his in-frame shots.

deviations_and_open_items.detail: The project's automatic rerun budget is 0. Nothing in this batch needed a rerun: no blocker was found, no route was redrawn, and nothing was patched around. Had a route conflict been real it would have been routed to orchestrator as a user decision rather than fixed here.
